questions.stem: A startup runs a short-lived EC2 workload with spiky, unpredictable traffic and wants no commitment or upfront cost. Which purchase option fits best?

explanation.correct: On-Demand charges per second/hour with no commitment or upfront payment, which suits short-lived, spiky, or unpredictable workloads.

distractors.A: Dedicated Hosts are the most expensive option and target per-socket/core licensing and compliance, not short, flexible workloads.
distractors.B: A Savings Plan commits you to a steady hourly spend for 1 or 3 years, which a startup with unpredictable traffic does not want.
distractors.D: Reserved Instances require a 1- or 3-year commitment — the opposite of 'no commitment' — and suit steady, predictable usage.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'No commitment / unpredictable / short-term' almost always points to On-Demand.

questions.stem: A data team runs fault-tolerant batch jobs that can tolerate interruptions and wants the deepest possible EC2 discount. Which purchase option fits?

explanation.correct: Spot Instances use spare AWS capacity at the deepest discount off On-Demand, but AWS can reclaim them on short notice — ideal for interruption-tolerant, flexible work like batch jobs.

distractors.A: Dedicated Hosts are the most expensive option, aimed at licensing and compliance, not savings.
distractors.B: On-Demand carries no discount, so it is the wrong choice when the goal is the deepest savings.
distractors.C: Reserved Instances discount steady, always-on usage via a 1- or 3-year commitment; they are not the deepest discount and waste commitment on interruptible batch work.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Fault-tolerant / interruptible + biggest discount' = Spot.

questions.stem: A company runs an always-on production database on EC2 for three years and wants the lowest steady-state cost through commitment. Which option?

explanation.correct: Reserved Instances give a significant discount in exchange for a 1- or 3-year commitment, which fits predictable, always-on usage like a production database.

distractors.A: On-Demand carries no commitment discount, so it costs more for steady, long-running workloads.
distractors.C: The Free Tier offers limited introductory usage for learning, not production capacity for a three-year database.
distractors.D: Spot Instances can be interrupted at any time, which is unacceptable for an always-on production database.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Steady / always-on / predictable + willing to commit' = Reserved Instances (or a Savings Plan).

questions.stem: An organization wants a discount spanning EC2, Fargate, and Lambda by committing to a steady hourly spend for one year. Which option?

explanation.correct: A Compute Savings Plan commits to a consistent hourly spend and applies the discount flexibly across EC2, AWS Fargate, and AWS Lambda, regardless of region or instance family.

distractors.B: Spot gives a deep discount but no steady commitment-based savings and can be interrupted; it is not a spend commitment.
distractors.C: Dedicated Hosts are a physical-server tenancy model for licensing, not a flexible compute discount.
distractors.D: Standard Reserved Instances apply to EC2 only and are tied to specific instance attributes — they do not cover Fargate or Lambda.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Flexible discount across EC2 + Fargate + Lambda for an hourly $ commitment' = Compute Savings Plan.

questions.stem: A learner wants AWS services that stay free beyond the first twelve months, within monthly limits, to keep practicing. Which AWS Free Tier category?

explanation.correct: The Always Free category of the AWS Free Tier offers usage that never expires, up to defined monthly limits, for as long as you have an account.

distractors.A: Free Trials are short-term and end after a set period once activated.
distractors.C: 'Reserved capacity' is a pricing-commitment idea, not a Free Tier category.
distractors.D: 12-Months Free offers expire 12 months after account sign-up, so they do not 'stay free beyond twelve months.'

explanation.exam_pattern: Free Tier has three buckets: Always Free (never expires), 12-Months Free (from sign-up), and short Free Trials.

questions.stem: A company must honor software licenses tied to physical cores and needs visibility into the underlying host for compliance. Which EC2 option?

explanation.correct: Dedicated Hosts give you a physical server dedicated to your account with visibility into sockets and cores, supporting bring-your-own-license (BYOL) models and compliance requirements.

distractors.B: Default shared tenancy places you on multi-tenant hardware with no visibility into the physical host.
distractors.C: Reserved Instances are a billing discount, not a tenancy or hardware-visibility model.
distractors.D: Spot Instances run on shared spare capacity and give no dedicated-hardware visibility or per-core licensing control.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Per-socket/core licensing (BYOL) or hardware visibility for compliance' = Dedicated Hosts.

questions.stem: A finance lead notices that committing to one- or three-year usage lowers the unit price versus hourly rates. Which AWS pricing principle is this?

explanation.correct: 'Pay less when you reserve' means committing to usage (Reserved Instances or Savings Plans) lowers the per-unit price compared with On-Demand rates.

distractors.A: AWS does not promise zero upfront payment; some reservations even offer an all-upfront option for a larger discount.
distractors.B: Pay-as-you-go describes paying only for what you use with no commitment — it does not explain the commitment discount.
distractors.C: 'Pay less by using more' refers to volume/tiered discounts as usage grows, a different mechanism than reserving.

explanation.exam_pattern: Commitment (1/3-year) lowering the rate = 'pay less when you reserve.'

references: AWS Cloud Value / How AWS Pricing Works

questions.stem: As a company stores progressively more data in Amazon S3, its per-GB rate drops at higher usage tiers. Which AWS pricing principle is this?

options.text: Pay less by using more (volume-based discounts)

explanation.correct: 'Pay less by using more' means higher aggregate usage reaches lower-priced tiers, as with Amazon S3's tiered per-GB storage pricing.

distractors.A: Pay-as-you-go describes paying for consumption; it does not by itself drop the unit rate as volume grows.
distractors.B: Reserving lowers price through a time commitment, not through greater volume.
distractors.D: Spot pricing is an EC2 spare-capacity model, unrelated to S3 tiered storage rates.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Rate falls as volume/usage rises' = 'pay less by using more.'

references: AWS Cloud Value / How AWS Pricing Works

questions.stem: A manager wants to visualize the last several months of AWS spend by service and forecast upcoming costs. Which tool fits?

explanation.correct: AWS Cost Explorer provides interactive graphs to analyze and visualize past spend and usage by dimensions like service, plus built-in forecasting of future costs.

distractors.B: AWS Budgets is for setting thresholds and sending alerts, not for exploring and visualizing historical spend by service.
distractors.C: The Cost and Usage Report delivers raw granular line items to S3; it is not an interactive visualization/forecast dashboard.
distractors.D: AWS Pricing Calculator estimates costs before deployment; it does not analyze incurred spend.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Visualize/analyze/forecast existing spend' = Cost Explorer.

questions.stem: A team wants an automatic email alert when monthly AWS spend is forecast to exceed a set dollar threshold. Which service?

explanation.correct: AWS Budgets lets you set custom cost or usage thresholds and triggers alerts when actual or forecasted spend crosses them.

distractors.A: Trusted Advisor gives best-practice checks (including cost optimization), not custom spend-threshold alerts.
distractors.B: Cost Explorer analyzes and forecasts spend for review but does not send threshold-based alerts.
distractors.D: Pricing Calculator estimates costs before you deploy; it does not monitor actual spend.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Alert me when spend crosses $X' = AWS Budgets.

questions.stem: Before launching a new architecture, an architect wants to estimate the monthly cost of planned EC2 and S3 usage. Which tool?

explanation.correct: AWS Pricing Calculator models and estimates costs for planned workloads before anything is deployed, so you can compare configurations up front.

distractors.A: Budgets tracks and alerts on actual or forecasted spend of running resources, not hypothetical designs.
distractors.C: The Cost and Usage Report details actual past usage, not pre-deployment estimates.
distractors.D: Cost Explorer analyzes spend that has already been incurred; it needs existing usage to report on.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Estimate before deploying / what-if cost' = Pricing Calculator.

questions.stem: An enterprise with many AWS accounts wants one monthly bill and combined usage to reach volume pricing tiers. Which capability?

explanation.correct: Consolidated billing in AWS Organizations combines member accounts under one payer with a single bill and aggregates usage so the group can reach volume pricing tiers — at no additional charge.

distractors.B: Pricing Calculator estimates costs; it does not combine account billing.
distractors.C: Budgets alerts on thresholds; it does not consolidate billing across accounts.
distractors.D: Cost allocation tags categorize and break down costs; they do not merge accounts onto one bill.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Many accounts → one bill + aggregated volume discounts' = consolidated billing via AWS Organizations.

questions.stem: A company must break its AWS bill down by department and project to charge costs back internally. Which feature enables this?

explanation.correct: Cost allocation tags (key/value labels on resources, activated in the Billing console) let you group and report costs by dimensions such as department or project for chargeback.

distractors.A: Consolidated billing combines accounts into one bill but does not itself split spend by department or project.
distractors.B: Pricing Calculator produces pre-deployment estimates, not categorized bill breakdowns.
distractors.D: Savings Plans are a discount commitment, unrelated to categorizing costs.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Break down / categorize the bill by team, project, environment' = cost allocation tags.

questions.stem: A FinOps analyst needs the most granular line-item billing data delivered to Amazon S3 for querying with Amazon Athena. Which resource?

explanation.correct: The AWS Cost and Usage Report is the most comprehensive, granular billing dataset; it drops detailed line items into S3 where tools like Athena, Redshift, or QuickSight can query them.

distractors.A: Pricing Calculator estimates future costs; it produces no billing data about actual usage.
distractors.B: Budgets focuses on threshold alerts, not detailed data delivery to S3.
distractors.C: Cost Explorer offers interactive summaries, not the most granular line-item export for external querying.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Most granular / line-item data to S3 for Athena' = Cost and Usage Report.

questions.stem: A company wants machine-learning-based detection of unusual spending spikes, with alerts when costs deviate from normal patterns. Which capability fits best?

explanation.correct: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection uses machine learning to learn normal spend patterns and alert you when usage or cost deviates unexpectedly.

distractors.A: Pricing Calculator estimates costs before deployment; it does not watch live spend for anomalies.
distractors.B: Compute Optimizer recommends right-sizing of resources for efficiency, not spend-anomaly alerting.
distractors.D: Cost allocation tags categorize spend; they do not detect anomalies.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'ML detects unusual/unexpected spend' = Cost Anomaly Detection.

questions.stem: A company wants to estimate costs before deploying and be alerted when actual monthly spend exceeds a threshold. Which two services? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: AWS Pricing Calculator covers the pre-deployment estimate, and AWS Budgets covers the alert when actual spend crosses the chosen threshold — together they meet both needs.

distractors.B: The Cost and Usage Report delivers granular historical billing data; it neither estimates future costs nor sends threshold alerts.
distractors.D: Trusted Advisor runs best-practice checks (including cost optimization) but does not estimate pre-deployment costs or send custom spend-threshold alerts.

explanation.exam_pattern: Split the ask: 'estimate first' = Pricing Calculator; 'alert on overspend' = Budgets.

questions.stem: A new account owner asks which AWS Support plan is included with every account at no additional cost. Which plan?

explanation.correct: Basic Support is free for all accounts and includes documentation, whitepapers, AWS re:Post, 24/7 account and billing customer service, and a limited set of Trusted Advisor checks.

distractors.A: Enterprise Support is the highest-cost paid tier.
distractors.B: Business Support is a paid tier.
distractors.C: Developer Support is a paid tier.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Included free with every account' = Basic Support.

questions.stem: A company needs 24/7 phone, chat, and email access to Cloud Support Engineers at the lowest-cost plan that offers it. Which plan?

explanation.correct: Business Support is the lowest tier that adds 24/7 access to Cloud Support Engineers by phone, chat, and email for production issues.

distractors.A: Enterprise Support includes 24/7 support but is higher cost, so it is not the lowest-cost plan that offers it.
distractors.B: Developer Support offers business-hours email access to Cloud Support Associates only — not 24/7, and not phone/chat engineer access.
distractors.D: Basic Support has no technical support; its 24/7 contact is for account and billing questions only.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Lowest plan with 24/7 technical support (phone/chat/email)' = Business.

questions.stem: A large enterprise wants a designated Technical Account Manager who provides proactive guidance and well-architected reviews. Which support plan includes this?

explanation.correct: Enterprise Support includes a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM) who gives proactive, account-specific guidance such as well-architected reviews and optimization help.

distractors.A: Developer Support is business-hours email support only, with no TAM.
distractors.B: Business Support provides 24/7 technical support but no designated TAM.
distractors.D: Basic Support offers no technical support and no TAM.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Designated TAM / concierge, proactive guidance' = Enterprise Support.

questions.stem: A developer testing in a non-production environment wants low-cost technical support by email during business hours. Which entry-level paid plan?

explanation.correct: Developer Support is the lowest-cost paid plan, offering business-hours email access to Cloud Support Associates — a fit for experimentation and non-production testing.

distractors.B: Enterprise On-Ramp is a much higher tier that adds TAM access and 24/7 support.
distractors.C: Business Support adds 24/7 engineer access at a higher cost than this use case requires.
distractors.D: Basic Support is free but provides no technical support at all, so it is not a paid plan with email tech support.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Cheapest paid plan, business-hours email, test/non-prod' = Developer Support.

questions.stem: A company wants 24/7 support and access to a pool of Technical Account Managers, below the cost of full Enterprise Support. Which plan?

explanation.correct: Enterprise On-Ramp sits between Business and Enterprise: it adds 24/7 support plus access to a pool of Technical Account Managers, at a lower cost than full Enterprise Support.

distractors.A: Business Support provides 24/7 support but no Technical Account Manager access.
distractors.B: Developer Support is business-hours email only, with no 24/7 or TAM access.
distractors.C: Basic Support has no technical support and no TAM access.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'TAM access (pool) + 24/7, but not full Enterprise' = Enterprise On-Ramp.

questions.stem: A customer opens an AWS Support case and asks what determines how quickly AWS targets its response. Which factor set applies?

options.text: How old the AWS account is
The AWS Region the resources run in
The number of IAM users in the account
The case severity combined with the support plan tier

explanation.correct: Targeted response times depend on the severity of the case and the support plan tier — higher tiers and more severe (e.g. business-critical) cases get faster response targets.

distractors.A: Account age has no bearing on support response targets.
distractors.B: The Region where resources run does not set support response times.
distractors.C: The count of IAM users is unrelated to support response times.

explanation.exam_pattern: Response speed scales with case severity and plan tier — not with region, account age, or user count.

questions.stem: A team wants the full set of AWS Trusted Advisor checks across all categories unlocked through their support plan. Which is the minimum plan required?

options.text: Any plan — all checks are always free

explanation.correct: The full set of Trusted Advisor checks is unlocked at Business Support and above (including Enterprise On-Ramp and Enterprise).

distractors.B: Developer Support still gets only the limited, core check set.
distractors.C: Only a limited set is free on Basic/Developer; the full set is gated behind Business+.
distractors.D: Basic Support gets only a limited set of Trusted Advisor checks.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Full Trusted Advisor checks' = Business tier or higher (Basic/Developer get a limited subset).

questions.stem: A company wants automated best-practice recommendations spanning cost, security, fault tolerance, performance, and service limits. Which AWS tool provides these?

explanation.correct: AWS Trusted Advisor inspects your environment and recommends improvements across categories such as cost optimization, security, fault tolerance, performance, and service limits.

distractors.A: CloudTrail records API activity for auditing; it is not a recommendations engine.
distractors.B: The AWS Health Dashboard reports the status of AWS service events; it does not run best-practice checks on your configuration.
distractors.D: Pricing Calculator estimates costs before deployment; it gives no best-practice checks.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Checks across cost/security/fault-tolerance/performance/limits' = Trusted Advisor.

questions.stem: An operations team wants personalized alerts about AWS events that affect its own account's resources, with remediation guidance. Which tool fits?

options.text: The public AWS service health status page

explanation.correct: The account-specific view of the AWS Health Dashboard (formerly the Personal Health Dashboard) gives personalized alerts and remediation guidance for AWS events that affect your own resources.

distractors.A: The public service health status page shows general, non-personalized service status, not events scoped to your resources.
distractors.B: Trusted Advisor runs best-practice checks; it is not a notification feed for AWS-side events.
distractors.D: CloudWatch monitors metrics, logs, and alarms you configure on your resources, not AWS-side operational events.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Personalized / affecting MY resources' = AWS Health Dashboard (account health); public status page = everyone's general status.

questions.stem: A developer wants a free, community-driven AWS question-and-answer service where AWS experts and other users respond. Which resource?

explanation.correct: AWS re:Post is a free, community-driven question-and-answer service (the successor to the AWS forums) where AWS experts and the community answer technical questions.

distractors.A: AWS Professional Services is a paid consulting organization, not a free community forum.
distractors.C: Business Support is a paid support plan, not a free community Q&A service.
distractors.D: AWS Marketplace is a catalog for buying third-party software, not a Q&A community.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Free community Q&A' = AWS re:Post.

questions.stem: A company wants to find, buy, and deploy third-party software, billed together with its AWS charges. Which resource fits?

explanation.correct: AWS Marketplace is a curated digital catalog where customers find, buy, and deploy third-party software, with charges appearing on their AWS bill.

distractors.A: AWS re:Post is a community Q&A service, not a software marketplace.
distractors.B: AWS Knowledge Center is a library of help articles, not a place to purchase software.
distractors.D: Trusted Advisor provides best-practice checks, not software procurement.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Buy/deploy third-party software billed through AWS' = AWS Marketplace.

questions.stem: A customer needs a vetted third-party consulting firm to help design and migrate its AWS workloads. Which program helps locate one?

explanation.correct: The AWS Partner Network is a global community of consulting and technology partners; customers use it to find vetted firms that help design, build, and migrate AWS workloads.

distractors.A: Trusted Advisor provides best-practice checks, not partner discovery.
distractors.C: AWS re:Post is a free community Q&A service, not a directory of consulting partners.
distractors.D: The Health Dashboard reports service/account event status, not partners.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Find a vetted partner / consulting firm' = AWS Partner Network.

questions.stem: A new user wants free articles that answer the most common AWS questions, without opening a support case. Which resource?

explanation.correct: The AWS Knowledge Center is a free library of articles and videos answering the most frequently asked AWS questions — no support case required.

distractors.A: AWS IQ connects you with paid, on-demand third-party experts, not free self-service articles.
distractors.B: Business Support is a paid support plan, not a free self-service article library.
distractors.D: AWS Professional Services is a paid consulting engagement.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Free self-service articles for common questions' = AWS Knowledge Center.

questions.stem: A team wants free AWS-authored whitepapers and best-practice guidance, such as the Well-Architected Framework, to inform its design. Which resource?

explanation.correct: AWS Whitepapers and documentation are free, authoritative technical resources — including the AWS Well-Architected Framework — that guide architecture and best-practice decisions.

distractors.A: AWS Marketplace sells third-party software; it is not AWS-authored guidance.
distractors.C: AWS Budgets sends spend/usage threshold alerts; it is not guidance documentation.
distractors.D: Cost Explorer analyzes and visualizes spend, not architectural best practices.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Free AWS-authored best-practice guidance / Well-Architected' = whitepapers and documentation.

questions.stem: A startup wants to avoid buying and owning servers up front and instead pay only for the compute capacity it actually consumes. Which cloud benefit is this?

options.text: Benefit from massive economies of scale
Trade fixed capital expense for variable expense

explanation.correct: Paying only for capacity you consume instead of purchasing hardware up front is the 'trade capital expense for variable expense' advantage: cost scales with actual use rather than being locked in before launch.

distractors.A: Economies of scale is about lower prices from AWS aggregating many customers' usage, not about the capital-to-variable payment shift itself.
distractors.C: Speed and agility is about provisioning resources fast to innovate, not the capital-versus-variable cost model.
distractors.D: Going global in minutes is about deploying to multiple Regions quickly, not about how you pay for resources.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Pay only for what you use / avoid up-front hardware purchase' = trade capital expense for variable expense.

references: AWS - Six Advantages of Cloud Computing (AWS Overview whitepaper)

questions.stem: Because AWS aggregates usage from hundreds of thousands of customers, it can offer lower pay-as-you-go prices than one company could achieve alone. Which benefit is this?

options.text: Trade capital expense for variable expense
Benefit from massive economies of scale

explanation.correct: Aggregated demand from many customers lets AWS achieve higher economies of scale and pass the savings on as lower pay-as-you-go prices.

distractors.A: Stopping capacity guesswork is about not having to predict infrastructure needs, not about pricing driven by aggregated demand.
distractors.B: The capital-to-variable shift changes how you pay; the lower unit price from scale is a separate advantage.
distractors.D: Elasticity is automatically adding and removing resources with demand, not the provider's pricing.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Aggregated customer demand leads to lower prices' = economies of scale.

references: AWS - Six Advantages of Cloud Computing (AWS Overview whitepaper)

questions.stem: An online store's traffic triples during a flash sale, then returns to normal; it automatically adds compute during the surge and releases it afterward. Which cloud characteristic is this?

explanation.correct: Elasticity is automatically acquiring resources as demand rises and releasing them as it falls, so you pay only for what the workload currently needs.

distractors.A: Durability describes how well stored data is protected from loss, not scaling compute with demand.
distractors.B: Fault tolerance is a system's ability to keep operating despite component failure, not matching capacity to changing load.
distractors.D: Economies of scale is about lower prices from aggregated demand, not automatic scaling to match load.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Automatically scale out under load and scale in when idle' = elasticity.

references: AWS - Overview of Amazon Web Services whitepaper (cloud computing concepts)

questions.stem: An enterprise is building its cloud business case. Which TWO of the following are advantages of cloud computing as described by AWS? (Choose two.)

options.text: Eliminate the customer's share of all security responsibilities
Guarantee that applications can never experience downtime

explanation.correct: Going global in minutes (deploying to multiple Regions quickly) and stopping capacity guesswork are two of AWS's stated advantages of cloud computing.

distractors.A: Security is a shared responsibility; AWS secures the cloud, but the customer always keeps responsibilities in the cloud, so the cloud never eliminates them.
distractors.B: No provider guarantees zero downtime; the cloud improves availability and resilience but does not promise perfect uptime.

explanation.exam_pattern: Watch for absolutes ('eliminate all', 'never', 'guarantee zero') - they are usually wrong cloud-benefit distractors.

references: AWS - Six Advantages of Cloud Computing (AWS Overview whitepaper)

questions.stem: A team that once waited weeks for hardware procurement can now launch new servers in minutes and experiment freely. Which cloud benefit does this illustrate?

options.text: Trade capital expense for variable expense

explanation.correct: Provisioning resources in minutes lowers the cost of experimenting and lets teams innovate and reach market faster - the speed and agility advantage.

distractors.B: The capital-to-variable shift is about how you pay, not how fast you can provision resources.
distractors.C: Durability is about protecting stored data from loss, unrelated to how quickly you can provision.
distractors.D: Economies of scale is about lower prices from aggregated demand, not provisioning speed.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Provision in minutes, experiment cheaply, faster time to market' = agility / speed.

references: AWS - Six Advantages of Cloud Computing (AWS Overview whitepaper)

questions.stem: A company wants to lower latency for customers in Europe and Asia by deploying its application close to them in several AWS Regions within minutes. Which benefit is this?

options.text: Trade capital expense for variable expense

explanation.correct: Deploying to multiple AWS Regions quickly to place the application near end users, lowering their latency, is the 'go global in minutes' advantage.

distractors.B: Elasticity is scaling capacity up and down with demand, not deploying across Regions for proximity to users.
distractors.C: Economies of scale is about pricing from aggregated demand, not multi-Region reach.
distractors.D: The capital-to-variable shift is about the payment model, not global deployment speed.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Deploy near users in multiple Regions to cut latency' = go global in minutes.

references: AWS - Six Advantages of Cloud Computing (AWS Overview whitepaper)

questions.stem: Before the cloud, a company often bought too many or too few servers because demand was hard to predict. How does cloud computing best address this problem?

options.text: It removes the need to monitor usage entirely
It requires forecasting peak demand accurately before launch
It lets the company scale capacity up or down on demand, so it stops guessing capacity
It guarantees a fixed block of capacity reserved years in advance

explanation.correct: The cloud lets you scale resources up or down as needed, so you no longer over- or under-provision - you 'stop guessing capacity'.

distractors.A: You still monitor usage; the cloud removes the guesswork, not the monitoring.
distractors.B: The cloud removes the need to forecast peak demand up front, the opposite of this option.
distractors.D: Reserving a fixed block of capacity years ahead is the old on-premises model the cloud replaces.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'No more over- or under-provisioning; scale with actual demand' = stop guessing capacity.

references: AWS - Six Advantages of Cloud Computing (AWS Overview whitepaper)

questions.stem: By moving to AWS, a business no longer racks servers, powers and cools a facility, or staffs data-center operations, and can focus on customers. Which benefit is this?

options.text: Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers

explanation.correct: Offloading the heavy lifting of data-center operations - racking, power, cooling, and staffing - so the business can focus on its differentiators is a core cloud advantage.

distractors.A: Economies of scale is about lower prices from aggregated demand, not removing facility operations from your plate.
distractors.C: Going global in minutes is about multi-Region deployment speed, not shedding data-center operating costs.
distractors.D: Elasticity is scaling with demand, not eliminating data-center operations.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Stop racking/powering/cooling servers; focus on the business' = stop spending on data centers (removing undifferentiated heavy lifting).

references: AWS - Six Advantages of Cloud Computing (AWS Overview whitepaper)

questions.stem: An architect deploys an application across multiple Availability Zones so it keeps running if one zone fails. Which cloud benefit is the team primarily pursuing?

explanation.correct: Spreading a workload across multiple Availability Zones so it survives a single-zone failure increases availability and resilience - a key benefit of building on the cloud.

distractors.B: Going global in minutes refers to multi-Region reach for users and latency; multiple AZs within one Region target availability.
distractors.C: Capital expenditure is up-front hardware spend - the opposite of a cloud advantage.
distractors.D: Multi-AZ deployment targets resilience, not reducing unit prices (that is economies of scale).

explanation.exam_pattern: Multiple AZs = survive a zone failure = high availability; multiple Regions = global reach / latency.

references: AWS - Global Infrastructure (Regions and Availability Zones)

questions.stem: An organization wants AWS best-practice guidance, organized into six pillars, to review and improve its cloud architectures over time. Which offering provides this?

explanation.correct: The AWS Well-Architected Framework provides best practices and questions across six pillars to help you build and review secure, reliable, efficient, cost-effective, and sustainable workloads.

distractors.A: Trusted Advisor is a tool that checks an account against best practices, but the six-pillar framework itself is the Well-Architected Framework.
distractors.B: AWS Organizations centrally manages multiple AWS accounts; it does not define architectural best-practice pillars.
distractors.C: The Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) guides organizational cloud adoption across six perspectives; it is not the architecture-review framework.

explanation.exam_pattern: Six pillars + architecture best practices/review = Well-Architected Framework (CAF is organizational adoption).

questions.stem: A team applies least-privilege permissions, encrypts data at rest and in transit, and enables traceability of actions. Which Well-Architected pillar do these practices serve?

explanation.correct: Protecting data, systems, and assets - least privilege, encryption, and traceability - is the focus of the Security pillar.

distractors.A: Reliability is about a workload performing correctly and recovering from failure, not access control or encryption.
distractors.C: Cost Optimization is about avoiding unnecessary spend, not protecting data.
distractors.D: Performance Efficiency is about using computing resources efficiently and selecting the right resource types.

explanation.exam_pattern: Least privilege, encryption, traceability, protect data = Security pillar.

questions.stem: A workload must automatically recover from failures, scale horizontally to meet demand, and have its recovery procedures tested regularly. Which pillar emphasizes this?

explanation.correct: Ensuring a workload performs its intended function correctly and recovers from failure - automatic recovery, horizontal scaling, and tested recovery - defines the Reliability pillar.

distractors.B: Security focuses on protecting data and systems, not recovery and scaling for availability.
distractors.C: Sustainability focuses on minimizing environmental impact, not recovery and availability.
distractors.D: Operational Excellence focuses on running and monitoring systems and continuously improving processes, not primarily failure recovery.

explanation.exam_pattern: Recover from failure, test recovery, scale horizontally = Reliability.

questions.stem: An architect selects the most suitable instance types, adopts serverless where possible, and experiments to use computing resources efficiently. Which pillar is this?

explanation.correct: Using computing resources efficiently - selecting the right resource types/sizes and adopting advanced technologies such as serverless - is the Performance Efficiency pillar.

distractors.A: Operational Excellence targets running, monitoring, and improving operations, not resource efficiency.
distractors.B: Cost Optimization targets eliminating unneeded spend; efficient selection can aid cost, but the stated goal here is efficient performance.
distractors.D: Reliability targets correct operation and recovery from failure, not efficient use of resources.

explanation.exam_pattern: Select the right/efficient resources, use serverless, experiment = Performance Efficiency.

references: AWS Well-Architected Framework - Performance Efficiency pillar

questions.stem: A team wants to avoid paying for idle resources, adopt a consumption model, and attribute spending to the teams that incur it. Which Well-Architected pillar is this?

explanation.correct: Avoiding unnecessary costs, adopting a consumption model, and attributing expenditure are core practices of the Cost Optimization pillar.

distractors.A: Sustainability is about reducing environmental impact; it can reduce cost but is not focused on managing expenditure.
distractors.B: Performance Efficiency is about using resources efficiently for performance, not controlling and attributing spend.
distractors.D: Operational Excellence is about operations and continuous improvement, not cost control.

explanation.exam_pattern: Eliminate idle spend, consumption model, cost attribution = Cost Optimization.

references: AWS Well-Architected Framework - Cost Optimization pillar

questions.stem: A study group lists candidates for the pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework. Which TWO of the following are actual pillars of the framework? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: Sustainability and Operational Excellence are two of the six Well-Architected pillars (the others are Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, and Cost Optimization).

distractors.A: Elasticity is a cloud characteristic and design principle, not one of the six named pillars.
distractors.D: Scalability is a cloud characteristic, not a pillar of the framework.

explanation.exam_pattern: Six pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Sustainability - elasticity/scalability are concepts, not pillars.

questions.stem: A team performs operations as code, makes frequent small reversible changes, and continuously improves its processes and procedures. Which pillar describes this?

explanation.correct: Running and monitoring systems while continuously improving processes - operations as code, with small frequent reversible changes - is the Operational Excellence pillar.

distractors.A: Reliability focuses on correct operation and recovery from failure, not operations-as-code and process improvement.
distractors.B: Security focuses on protecting data and systems.
distractors.C: Cost Optimization focuses on avoiding unnecessary spend.

explanation.exam_pattern: Operations as code, small reversible changes, continuous improvement = Operational Excellence.

references: AWS Well-Architected Framework - Operational Excellence pillar

questions.stem: An architect wants to reduce a workload's environmental impact by maximizing resource utilization and using efficient managed services. Which pillar is this?

explanation.correct: Minimizing environmental impact - by maximizing utilization and using efficient managed services - is the Sustainability pillar, added to the framework in 2021.

distractors.B: Cost Optimization targets spend; higher utilization can cut cost, but reducing environmental impact is the Sustainability aim.
distractors.C: Performance Efficiency targets efficient performance, not environmental footprint.
distractors.D: Reliability targets correct operation and recovery, not sustainability.

explanation.exam_pattern: Minimize environmental impact, maximize utilization = Sustainability pillar.

questions.stem: To improve resilience, an architect removes a tight dependency between two components by placing a message queue between them so one can fail without stopping the other. Which design principle is applied?

options.text: Treat servers as pets, not cattle

explanation.correct: Loosely coupling components - for example by using a queue between them - so one component's failure is isolated is a core AWS design principle that improves reliability and scalability.

distractors.A: Scaling vertically only caps growth at one instance's size; AWS best practice favors horizontal scaling for resilience.
distractors.B: 'Pets, not cattle' is the opposite of the best practice; you treat servers as disposable (cattle), not unique and irreplaceable (pets).
distractors.D: Over-provisioning fixed capacity is the on-premises approach the cloud's elasticity replaces, not a resilience design principle.

explanation.exam_pattern: Queue / loose coupling so one failure does not cascade = decouple; disposable resources = design for failure.

questions.stem: To meet a data-center exit deadline, a company moves its applications to AWS as-is, with no code changes, to migrate quickly. Which migration strategy is this?

explanation.correct: Rehosting ('lift and shift') moves applications to the cloud without changing them - the fastest way to migrate, often ahead of later optimization.

distractors.A: Repurchasing replaces the app with a different product, typically SaaS, rather than moving it unchanged.
distractors.B: Retiring decommissions applications that are no longer needed, not moving them.
distractors.C: Refactoring re-architects the application (for example to cloud-native microservices), which takes much more time and change.

explanation.exam_pattern: Move as-is, no changes, fast = rehost (lift and shift).

questions.stem: While migrating, a team keeps its application's core architecture but moves its self-managed database onto Amazon RDS to cut admin effort. Which strategy is this?

explanation.correct: Replatforming makes a few cloud optimizations - such as moving to a managed database - for clear benefit, without changing the application's core architecture.

distractors.A: Rehosting moves the app entirely as-is, with no optimizations like switching to a managed database.
distractors.B: Refactoring fundamentally re-architects the application, far more change than a managed-database swap.
distractors.C: Retain means leaving the application where it is for now, not migrating and optimizing it.

explanation.exam_pattern: A few optimizations (for example a managed DB) but the same core architecture = replatform.

questions.stem: A company decides to drop its self-hosted CRM and move to a commercial SaaS CRM subscription instead. Which of the 6 R's migration strategies is this?

explanation.correct: Repurchasing ('drop and shop') replaces an existing application by moving to a different product, commonly a SaaS offering.

distractors.A: Replatforming optimizes the same application; it does not switch to a different purchased product.
distractors.B: Rehosting moves the existing application to the cloud unchanged, not to a new SaaS product.
distractors.D: Retain leaves the application in place; here the company is actively changing products.

explanation.exam_pattern: Switch to a different product, usually SaaS = repurchase (drop and shop).

questions.stem: To gain scalability, a team redesigns a monolith into microservices using managed and serverless AWS services rather than moving it unchanged. Which migration strategy is this?

explanation.correct: Refactoring (re-architecting) reimagines how the application is built - often cloud-native microservices or serverless - to gain scalability and agility, and is the most involved strategy.

distractors.A: Rehosting moves the app as-is; it does not redesign the architecture.
distractors.C: Retiring decommissions an application; here the team is rebuilding it, not removing it.
distractors.D: Replatforming makes only minor optimizations, not a full redesign into microservices.

explanation.exam_pattern: Redesign to cloud-native (microservices/serverless) for scalability = refactor / re-architect (most effort).

questions.stem: During migration planning, a company finds several applications that are no longer used and decides to decommission them. Which of the 6 R's is this?

explanation.correct: Retiring means decommissioning applications that are no longer needed, which reduces cost and attack surface during a migration.

distractors.A: Retain means keeping an application as-is (often on-premises) for now, not decommissioning it.
distractors.C: Rehosting moves an application to the cloud; retiring removes it instead.
distractors.D: Repurchasing swaps to a different product; retiring eliminates the application entirely.

explanation.exam_pattern: Turn off / decommission unused apps = retire; keep-for-now = retain.

questions.stem: A legacy application cannot move yet due to a vendor dependency, so the company leaves it on-premises and plans to revisit it later. Which migration strategy is this?

explanation.correct: Retaining means keeping an application in its current environment for now - for example due to a dependency or timing - and revisiting the decision later.

distractors.A: Refactoring re-architects the app in the cloud; retaining leaves it untouched on-premises.
distractors.B: Retiring decommissions an app that is no longer needed; here the app is still used and kept.
distractors.C: Rehosting moves the app to the cloud now; retaining deliberately does not move it yet.

explanation.exam_pattern: Keep as-is for now / not ready to move = retain; remove entirely = retire.

questions.stem: A company must move a large dataset to AWS from a site with slow, unreliable internet, where uploading over the network would take months. Which approach fits best?

options.text: Enable Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration over the existing link
Email the dataset to AWS Support
Use an AWS Snow Family device to transfer the data physically

explanation.correct: The AWS Snow Family provides physical devices to transfer large datasets offline when network bandwidth is limited or an online transfer would take too long; you load the device and ship it to AWS.

distractors.A: VPC peering connects two VPCs' networks; it does not move an on-premises dataset into AWS.
distractors.B: S3 Transfer Acceleration still relies on the internet link, which is too slow and unreliable in this scenario.
distractors.C: Emailing a large dataset is not a real transfer mechanism and is infeasible.

explanation.exam_pattern: Large dataset + limited bandwidth + offline/physical shipping = AWS Snow Family.

questions.stem: An organization wants a structured way to plan its cloud journey across business and technical areas, organized into six perspectives. Which AWS framework provides this?

explanation.correct: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) offers guidance to plan and accelerate cloud adoption, organizing capabilities into six perspectives: Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security, and Operations.

distractors.A: The Well-Architected Framework guides workload and architecture design across six pillars, not organizational adoption perspectives.
distractors.C: AWS Config records and evaluates resource configurations; it is not an adoption-planning framework.
distractors.D: AWS Service Catalog manages catalogs of approved IT products; it is not an adoption framework.

explanation.exam_pattern: Six perspectives + plan organizational cloud adoption = CAF (six pillars + architecture = Well-Architected).

questions.stem: A CAF assessment flags gaps in staff skills, roles, and change management for cloud adoption. Which AWS CAF perspective most directly addresses these concerns?

explanation.correct: The People perspective focuses on culture, organizational structure, roles, and skills - bridging technology and business during cloud adoption.

distractors.B: The Platform perspective addresses building and modernizing a scalable cloud platform and its workloads, not staff skills.
distractors.C: The Business perspective ensures cloud investments align with and accelerate business outcomes, not specifically skills and roles.
distractors.D: The Operations perspective ensures cloud services are run and managed to meet business needs, not workforce development.

explanation.exam_pattern: Skills, roles, culture, change management = People perspective of the CAF.

references: AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) - perspectives

questions.stem: Moving to AWS lets a company stop making large up-front hardware purchases and instead pay an ongoing variable bill for what it uses. Which shift does this represent?

explanation.correct: The cloud converts large up-front capital expenditure on hardware into ongoing, variable operational expenditure that scales with usage - a shift from CapEx to OpEx.

distractors.A: This reverses the actual shift; the cloud moves spending away from CapEx, not toward it.
distractors.B: A sunk cost is money already spent and unrecoverable; pay-as-you-go is the opposite of locking in sunk costs.
distractors.C: Reserved pricing is a commitment-based discount model, not the CapEx-to-OpEx concept described.

explanation.exam_pattern: Up-front hardware purchase (CapEx) becomes a pay-as-you-go variable bill (OpEx).

questions.stem: An analytics team runs large jobs only a few hours each week and pays solely for the compute time those jobs consume. Which pricing principle is this?

explanation.correct: Pay-as-you-go means paying only for the resources you consume, for as long as you use them, with no large up-front commitment - ideal for intermittent workloads.

distractors.B: Flat annual licensing charges a fixed fee regardless of usage, unlike consumption-based pricing.
distractors.C: Economies of scale is about lower unit prices from aggregated demand, not the pay-only-for-use model.
distractors.D: An up-front capital purchase pays for capacity in advance, the opposite of paying only for what you use.

explanation.exam_pattern: Pay only for what you use, when you use it = pay-as-you-go / consumption pricing.

questions.stem: A review finds many EC2 instances running at under ten percent utilization, so a team switches them to smaller instance types to cut cost. Which cost practice is this?

explanation.correct: Right-sizing matches instance types and sizes to actual workload requirements, so you pay for the capacity you need rather than for idle, oversized resources.

distractors.B: Vertical sharding is a data-partitioning technique, unrelated to matching instance size to load.
distractors.C: Lift and shift (rehost) is a migration strategy, not a cost-optimization resizing practice.
distractors.D: Over-provisioning is allocating more capacity than needed - the problem being fixed here, not the fix.

explanation.exam_pattern: Match resource size to actual usage to cut waste = right-sizing.

questions.stem: Before migrating, a company wants to estimate what a workload will cost to run on AWS so it can compare against its own data center. Which AWS tool helps model this?

explanation.correct: The AWS Pricing Calculator lets you estimate the cost of AWS services up front, producing the AWS-side figure you use in a total-cost-of-ownership comparison before you migrate.

distractors.A: AWS Cost Explorer analyzes your past and current AWS spend, not the cost of a workload you have not yet deployed.
distractors.C: Amazon CloudWatch monitors operational metrics and logs; it does not estimate pre-migration costs.
distractors.D: AWS Budgets alerts you when actual or forecast spend crosses a threshold; it does not model costs before migration.

explanation.exam_pattern: Estimate future AWS cost before deploying = AWS Pricing Calculator; analyze existing spend = Cost Explorer.

questions.stem: A finance lead notes that AWS's per-unit prices tend to fall as AWS serves more customers and gains greater purchasing power. Which economic concept explains this?

explanation.correct: Economies of scale means higher aggregate usage lets AWS buy and operate at lower unit cost and pass the savings on as lower pay-as-you-go prices.

distractors.B: Total cost of ownership is the full cost of owning and operating a solution, not why unit prices fall with scale.
distractors.C: Capital expenditure is up-front spending on assets, unrelated to volume-driven price reductions.
distractors.D: Right-sizing matches resources to workload needs; it does not explain provider-wide price drops.

explanation.exam_pattern: Lower unit prices because the provider operates at massive scale = economies of scale.

references: AWS - Six Advantages of Cloud Computing (economies of scale)

questions.stem: When comparing on-premises and cloud, a CFO wants a cost figure that includes hardware, power, cooling, space, and staff. Which measure captures all of these?

explanation.correct: Total cost of ownership captures the complete cost of a solution - hardware, facilities, power, cooling, and labor - enabling a fair on-premises-versus-cloud comparison.

distractors.B: Marginal utility is an economics concept about added satisfaction per unit, unrelated to cost comparison.
distractors.C: Capital expense alone omits ongoing operational costs such as power, cooling, and staff.
distractors.D: List price is only the headline price of a product, excluding operating and facility costs.

explanation.exam_pattern: All-in cost (hardware + facilities + power + staff) for comparison = total cost of ownership.

references: AWS - Cloud economics (Total Cost of Ownership)

questions.stem: By using AWS managed services, a team spends less staff time on patching, backups, and hardware upkeep and more on product features. Which cost benefit is this?

explanation.correct: Offloading routine infrastructure tasks - patching, backups, hardware upkeep - to AWS managed services removes 'undifferentiated heavy lifting', freeing staff to focus on work that differentiates the business.

distractors.A: Managed services reduce, not increase, capital expenditure.
distractors.B: Operational cost is reduced and shifted, not entirely eliminated - you still pay for the managed services you consume.
distractors.D: This benefit works alongside economies of scale; it does not avoid them.

explanation.exam_pattern: Let AWS handle routine infrastructure chores so staff focus on the business = removing undifferentiated heavy lifting.

references: AWS - Cloud economics (operational efficiency / managed services)

questions.stem: A company stops paying for servers that sit idle overnight because it can shut the resources down and is no longer billed while they are off. Which cost advantage is this?

options.text: Paying only for resources you consume (variable cost)

explanation.correct: With the cloud's consumption model you can turn resources off when idle and stop paying for them, converting the fixed cost of idle capacity into a variable cost tied to actual use.

distractors.B: Fixed cost regardless of usage describes owned on-premises hardware, not the cloud's variable model.
distractors.C: Economies of scope refers to savings from producing varied goods together; it is not this pay-for-use advantage.
distractors.D: Pay-as-you-go requires no mandatory multi-year commitment to benefit from stopping idle resources.

explanation.exam_pattern: Turn it off and stop paying = variable / consumption cost (versus the fixed cost of owned hardware).

references: AWS - Cloud economics (variable versus fixed cost)

questions.stem: A manager is sorting IT spending into categories. Which of the following is an example of operational expenditure (OpEx) rather than capital expenditure (CapEx)?

options.text: Purchasing physical servers for a new data center
A monthly, usage-based bill for the AWS compute consumed

explanation.correct: OpEx is ongoing operating spend; a monthly, usage-based AWS bill is OpEx. The other choices are one-time up-front asset purchases or builds, which are CapEx.

distractors.A: Constructing a data-center building is a large capital expenditure.
distractors.B: Buying physical servers is an up-front asset purchase - capital expenditure.
distractors.C: Purchasing networking hardware up front is a capital expenditure.

explanation.exam_pattern: Recurring usage-based spend = OpEx; one-time asset purchase or build = CapEx.

questions.stem: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, which party is responsible for the physical security of AWS data centers?

explanation.correct: AWS is responsible for 'security OF the cloud,' which includes the physical security of its data centers and global infrastructure.

distractors.A: The customer manages 'security IN the cloud' (data and configuration), not the physical facilities.
distractors.C: Auditors verify AWS's controls but are not responsible for operating physical security.
distractors.D: Physical data-center security is solely AWS's responsibility, not a shared duty.

explanation.exam_pattern: Physical, hardware, and facility wording points to AWS ('security OF the cloud').

questions.stem: A company runs applications on Amazon EC2 instances. Under the Shared Responsibility Model, who must patch the guest operating system?

options.text: The EC2 service patches it automatically

explanation.correct: For EC2 (an IaaS offering), the customer manages the guest OS, including applying patches and updates.

distractors.A: AWS Support can advise but does not patch customer instances.
distractors.B: AWS patches the host infrastructure and hypervisor, but not the customer's guest OS on EC2.
distractors.C: EC2 does not automatically patch the guest OS; that is left to the customer.

explanation.exam_pattern: EC2 (IaaS) plus guest OS or patching = customer responsibility.

questions.stem: In the Shared Responsibility Model, which item is always the customer's responsibility, regardless of which AWS service is used?

options.text: Managing their own data and its classification

explanation.correct: Customer data and its classification are always the customer's responsibility ('security IN the cloud').

distractors.A: The hypervisor and virtualization layer are maintained by AWS.
distractors.B: Secure disposal of storage media is handled by AWS.
distractors.C: Physical hardware security is AWS's responsibility (security OF the cloud).

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Customer data' is owned by the customer in every service model.

questions.stem: A customer moves from self-managing a database on EC2 to the managed Amazon RDS service. Which task does AWS now take over?

options.text: Choosing which data to store in the database
Creating database users and granting data access
Patching the underlying database engine and operating system

explanation.correct: With managed Amazon RDS, AWS handles the underlying operating system and database engine patching.

distractors.A: The customer always controls their own data.
distractors.B: Database users and data-level access remain the customer's responsibility.
distractors.C: Security group (firewall) configuration stays with the customer.

explanation.exam_pattern: A managed service shifts OS/engine patching to AWS; data and access stay with the customer.

questions.stem: Which TWO of the following are customer responsibilities under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model? (Choose two.)

options.text: Patching the guest operating system on EC2 instances
Maintaining the hardware that runs AWS services
Managing physical access to AWS data centers

explanation.correct: Configuring security groups and patching the EC2 guest OS are both 'security IN the cloud' tasks owned by the customer.

distractors.B: Maintaining the underlying hardware is AWS's responsibility.
distractors.D: Physical access to data centers is AWS's responsibility (security OF the cloud).

explanation.exam_pattern: On 'choose two' responsibility items, pick what you configure or run inside your own account.

questions.stem: A developer runs code on AWS Lambda. Under the Shared Responsibility Model, what remains the customer's responsibility?

options.text: The function code and the IAM permissions it uses
Patching the operating system that runs the function

explanation.correct: With Lambda, AWS manages the operating system and compute; the customer is responsible for their function code and the IAM permissions it uses.

distractors.B: AWS automatically scales the Lambda execution environment.
distractors.C: For Lambda, AWS manages and patches the underlying operating system.
distractors.D: AWS manages the underlying compute fleet for Lambda.

explanation.exam_pattern: Serverless (Lambda): the customer owns the code and access; AWS owns the rest.

questions.stem: Which of the following is handled by AWS, not the customer, under the Shared Responsibility Model?

options.text: Securely disposing of decommissioned storage hardware

explanation.correct: Secure disposal and decommissioning of storage hardware is AWS's responsibility.

distractors.A: Guest OS firewall configuration is the customer's job.
distractors.B: Choosing and applying encryption to customer data is a customer responsibility.
distractors.C: IAM user and permission management belongs to the customer.

explanation.exam_pattern: Hardware lifecycle and media disposal belong to AWS.

questions.stem: Under the Shared Responsibility Model, who is responsible for choosing and configuring how customer data is encrypted, both in transit and at rest?

options.text: AWS, because encryption is part of the managed infrastructure
The customer, who controls encryption of their data
No one; data in AWS cannot be customer-encrypted

explanation.correct: The customer decides on and configures how their data is encrypted, in transit and at rest, even when using managed services.

distractors.A: AWS secures the infrastructure, but the customer configures data encryption choices.
distractors.B: Auditors verify controls; they do not configure a customer's encryption.
distractors.D: AWS services support both in-transit and at-rest encryption.

explanation.exam_pattern: Encryption choices for your data are a customer responsibility.

questions.stem: An auditor asks a company to prove that OS patches are current on its EC2 fleet. Under the Shared Responsibility Model, who must maintain those patches?

options.text: Amazon Inspector, which applies the patches automatically
AWS, as part of security of the cloud
The customer, as part of security in the cloud

explanation.correct: Guest OS patching on EC2 is the customer's responsibility ('security IN the cloud').

distractors.A: Amazon Inspector assesses instances for vulnerabilities but does not apply patches.
distractors.B: AWS staff do not patch customer-managed guest operating systems.
distractors.C: AWS patches the underlying host, not the customer's guest OS on EC2.

explanation.exam_pattern: If it runs inside your EC2 instance, you are responsible for patching it.

questions.stem: In the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, the phrase 'security of the cloud' describes whose responsibilities?

explanation.correct: 'Security OF the cloud' describes AWS's responsibility for the infrastructure that runs all AWS services.

distractors.A: 'Managed service provider' is not a party defined in the model.
distractors.B: End users are not a party defined in the model.
distractors.C: The customer handles 'security IN the cloud' (data, IAM, configuration).

explanation.exam_pattern: 'OF the cloud' = AWS; 'IN the cloud' = customer.

questions.stem: Which AWS service provides on-demand access to AWS compliance reports such as SOC and PCI DSS documents?

explanation.correct: AWS Artifact is the self-service portal for on-demand AWS compliance reports and agreements.

distractors.A: AWS Trusted Advisor gives best-practice recommendations, not compliance reports.
distractors.B: AWS Config tracks resource configurations, not compliance report downloads.
distractors.D: AWS CloudTrail records API activity, not downloadable compliance reports.

explanation.exam_pattern: Need an AWS compliance report or certification document = AWS Artifact.

questions.stem: A healthcare provider must review and accept a Business Associate Addendum (BAA) with AWS for HIPAA workloads. Where is this agreement available?

explanation.correct: AWS Artifact provides AWS agreements, such as the BAA, which customers can review and accept online.

distractors.A: Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data in S3; it does not host agreements.
distractors.B: AWS Secrets Manager stores and rotates secrets, not legal agreements.
distractors.C: AWS Audit Manager automates evidence collection but does not host the BAA.

explanation.exam_pattern: AWS online agreements (BAA/NDA) are reviewed and accepted in AWS Artifact.

questions.stem: A security team needs a record of who made each API call in their AWS account, for auditing. Which service should they use?

explanation.correct: AWS CloudTrail records API calls and account activity for governance, compliance, and auditing.

distractors.A: AWS Artifact provides compliance documents, not account activity logs.
distractors.B: AWS Config tracks resource configuration state, not who called each API.
distractors.C: Amazon CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs for performance, not an API audit trail.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Who did what, and when' via API history = AWS CloudTrail.

questions.stem: A governance team wants to continuously evaluate whether resource configurations meet internal rules and track configuration changes over time. Which service fits best?

explanation.correct: AWS Config records resource configurations, tracks changes over time, and evaluates them against desired rules.

distractors.A: AWS CloudTrail logs API calls, not the configuration state of resources.
distractors.C: Amazon Inspector assesses software vulnerabilities, not configuration compliance.
distractors.D: AWS Shield protects against DDoS attacks.

explanation.exam_pattern: Resource configuration compliance and history = AWS Config.

questions.stem: An investigator must determine which IAM user deleted a specific resource and exactly when it happened. Which service provides this?

explanation.correct: AWS CloudTrail logs the identity, action, and timestamp of API calls, so it shows who deleted the resource and when.

distractors.A: AWS Config shows configuration state and changes but not the user identity behind each API call.
distractors.C: AWS Audit Manager automates evidence collection, not per-action user attribution.
distractors.D: AWS Artifact provides compliance reports, not account activity.

explanation.exam_pattern: User identity plus time of an action = CloudTrail; resource state over time = Config.

questions.stem: Which AWS service continuously assesses risk and automates the collection of evidence to help prepare for audits against frameworks and regulations?

explanation.correct: AWS Audit Manager continuously audits AWS usage and automates evidence collection to simplify compliance assessments.

distractors.A: AWS CloudTrail logs API activity but does not map evidence to compliance frameworks.
distractors.C: Amazon GuardDuty is a threat-detection service.
distractors.D: AWS Artifact only provides pre-built reports and agreements, not automated evidence collection.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Automate audit evidence collection' = AWS Audit Manager.

questions.stem: A company must ensure its customer data is stored only within a specific country to meet data-residency rules. Which AWS capability lets it control this?

options.text: Selecting the AWS Region where resources are deployed
Choosing a larger EC2 instance type

explanation.correct: Customers choose the Region, and AWS does not move their data out of it without consent, which supports data residency and sovereignty requirements.

distractors.A: Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data but does not control its geographic location.
distractors.B: AWS Shield Advanced provides DDoS protection, not control over data location.
distractors.D: Instance size has no effect on where data is stored.

explanation.exam_pattern: Data residency and sovereignty = the customer's choice of Region.

questions.stem: AWS maintains compliance with programs such as PCI DSS, ISO 27001, and SOC. How can a customer obtain proof of these certifications?

options.text: Open a support case with AWS Shield
Download the audit reports from AWS Artifact
Query the account with Amazon Athena
Enable AWS WAF on the account

explanation.correct: AWS Artifact provides the certification and attestation reports that demonstrate AWS's compliance.

distractors.A: AWS Shield is a DDoS protection service, unrelated to compliance reports.
distractors.C: Amazon Athena queries data in S3; it does not supply AWS's compliance reports.
distractors.D: AWS WAF filters web traffic and does not provide certifications.

explanation.exam_pattern: Proof of AWS's certifications = reports in AWS Artifact.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes how compliance works under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model?

options.text: AWS is fully responsible for the customer's compliance
Compliance is owned entirely by third-party auditors
AWS certifies the infrastructure, while the customer is responsible for compliance of what they build in the cloud
The customer is responsible for the data center's compliance

explanation.correct: Compliance is shared: AWS certifies the underlying infrastructure, and customers are responsible for their own workloads and data meeting requirements.

distractors.A: Customers remain responsible for their own workloads meeting requirements; AWS does not own it fully.
distractors.B: Auditors verify compliance, but responsibility is shared between AWS and the customer.
distractors.D: The customer does not run or certify AWS's physical data centers.

explanation.exam_pattern: Compliance is shared, just like security.

questions.stem: A company must show auditors a timeline of how one security group's rules changed over the past month. Which service provides this configuration history?

explanation.correct: AWS Config records configuration snapshots and a timeline of changes for resources such as security groups.

distractors.A: AWS CloudTrail shows the API calls that made changes, but not a configuration-state timeline per resource.
distractors.B: AWS Trusted Advisor gives recommendations, not a configuration timeline.
distractors.C: AWS Artifact supplies compliance documents, not resource change history.

explanation.exam_pattern: Configuration change history or timeline for a resource = AWS Config.

questions.stem: Which TWO actions are AWS-recommended best practices for protecting the account root user? (Choose two.)

options.text: Avoid using root access keys and remove them if they exist
Store the root password in the application source code
Use the root user for all daily administrative work
Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) on the root user

explanation.correct: Enabling MFA on root and avoiding/removing root access keys are both recommended protections for this highly privileged identity.

distractors.B: Storing the root password in source code exposes it and is never recommended.
distractors.C: The root user should not be used for routine tasks; create IAM identities instead.

explanation.exam_pattern: Root best-practice 'choose two' items usually pair MFA with removing root access keys.

questions.stem: An application on an EC2 instance needs to read objects from an Amazon S3 bucket. What is the most secure way to grant this access?

options.text: Embed the root user's access keys in the application
Make the S3 bucket publicly readable
Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instance
Hard-code an IAM user's access keys in the application

explanation.correct: An IAM role attached to the instance supplies temporary credentials automatically, with no long-term keys to manage.

distractors.A: Root access keys should never be used in applications.
distractors.B: Making the bucket public exposes the data to everyone on the internet.
distractors.D: Hard-coding long-term access keys is insecure and hard to rotate.

explanation.exam_pattern: An app on EC2 needing AWS access = attach an IAM role, not stored keys.

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of an IAM group?

options.text: To attach permissions to a collection of IAM users at once
To provide DDoS protection for applications
To store and manage encryption keys
To record API calls for auditing

explanation.correct: An IAM group lets you attach policies to many users at once, which simplifies permission management.

distractors.B: DDoS protection is provided by AWS Shield.
distractors.C: Managing encryption keys is the job of AWS KMS.
distractors.D: Recording API calls is done by AWS CloudTrail.

explanation.exam_pattern: IAM group = manage permissions for many users together.

questions.stem: A security policy states that each user should receive only the permissions required to perform their job. Which security principle does this describe?

explanation.correct: Granting only the permissions needed to do a job is the principle of least privilege.

distractors.A: Defense in depth refers to layering multiple security controls, not scoping permissions.
distractors.B: Shared responsibility splits duties between AWS and the customer.
distractors.D: Elasticity is a scaling concept, not a security principle.

explanation.exam_pattern: 'Only the permissions needed' = principle of least privilege.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly contrasts IAM access keys with a console password?

options.text: Access keys are for programmatic access (CLI, SDK, API); a password signs a user in to the console
Passwords are used by the CLI and access keys by the console
Access keys can be created only for the root user
Both are used only for physical data-center entry

explanation.correct: Access keys authenticate programmatic requests (CLI, SDK, API), while a password signs a user in to the console.

distractors.B: This reverses their roles: the CLI uses access keys, and the console uses a password.
distractors.C: IAM users, not only the root user, can have access keys.
distractors.D: Neither credential is used for physical facility access.

explanation.exam_pattern: Programmatic access = access keys; human console sign-in = password.

questions.stem: In AWS IAM, what does a policy define?

options.text: The hourly price of an EC2 instance
The permissions that allow or deny specific actions on specific resources
The encryption algorithm used by AWS KMS
The physical location of a data center

explanation.correct: An IAM policy is a JSON document that defines permissions, specifying allowed or denied actions on resources.

distractors.A: Pricing is not defined by IAM policies.
distractors.C: Encryption algorithms are not set by IAM policies.
distractors.D: Data-center location is unrelated to an IAM policy.

explanation.exam_pattern: IAM policy = a JSON document of allowed/denied actions on resources.

questions.stem: An organization wants employees to sign in once and gain access to multiple AWS accounts and business applications. Which service supports this?

options.text: AWS IAM Identity Center (successor to AWS SSO)

explanation.correct: AWS IAM Identity Center provides single sign-on access to multiple AWS accounts and applications.

distractors.A: AWS Artifact provides compliance documents.
distractors.C: Amazon GuardDuty is a threat-detection service.
distractors.D: AWS KMS manages encryption keys, not single sign-on.

explanation.exam_pattern: Single sign-on across multiple accounts/apps = IAM Identity Center.

questions.stem: Why is the AWS account root user considered especially sensitive and in need of protection?

options.text: It has complete, unrestricted access to every service and resource in the account
It can only view billing information
It has no permissions until policies are attached
It is automatically disabled after account sign-up

explanation.correct: The root user has full, unrestricted access to everything in the account, so it must be tightly protected.

distractors.B: The root user can do far more than view billing.
distractors.C: The root user starts with full access, not none.
distractors.D: The root user is not automatically disabled.

explanation.exam_pattern: Root = unlimited account power, so lock it down.

questions.stem: Which IAM identity is designed to be assumed by a trusted entity, such as an AWS service, and supplies temporary credentials?

options.text: A long-term access key stored in code

explanation.correct: An IAM role is assumed by trusted entities (services, users, applications) and grants temporary credentials.

distractors.A: An IAM group organizes users and their permissions; it is not assumed and issues no credentials.
distractors.B: The root user is a permanent, highly privileged identity, not a temporary role.
distractors.C: A stored access key is a long-term credential, not a role that grants temporary access.

explanation.exam_pattern: Temporary credentials for a trusted entity = IAM role.

questions.stem: A startup discovers it is using the root user's access keys inside a deployment script. Following AWS best practices, what should it do?

options.text: Share the root keys with more developers for convenience
Remove the root access keys and switch to an IAM role or IAM user with least privilege
Commit the root keys to a public repository
Keep the root keys but turn off MFA

explanation.correct: Best practice is to avoid root access keys entirely: remove them and use an IAM role or IAM user scoped with least privilege.

distractors.A: Sharing root keys widens the blast radius of a compromise.
distractors.C: Publishing keys publicly is a severe security breach.
distractors.D: Disabling MFA weakens security instead of improving it.

explanation.exam_pattern: Root access keys in use = remove them and switch to an IAM role or user.

questions.stem: Which AWS service is used to create and manage the cryptographic keys that encrypt data across AWS services?

explanation.correct: AWS KMS creates and manages cryptographic keys and controls their use for encryption across AWS services.

distractors.A: AWS WAF filters malicious web traffic.
distractors.B: Amazon GuardDuty is a threat-detection service.
distractors.D: AWS Shield provides DDoS protection.

explanation.exam_pattern: Create and manage encryption keys = AWS KMS.

questions.stem: A public-facing web application is being overwhelmed by a distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack. Which AWS service is designed to help defend against this?

explanation.correct: AWS Shield is a managed service specifically for protecting against DDoS attacks.

distractors.A: Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data in S3.
distractors.B: Amazon Inspector assesses workloads for software vulnerabilities.
distractors.C: AWS Secrets Manager stores and rotates secrets.

explanation.exam_pattern: DDoS protection = AWS Shield.

questions.stem: A team wants to block common web exploits such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting before they reach an application. Which service should they use?

explanation.correct: AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall) filters HTTP(S) requests and blocks common web exploits like SQL injection and XSS.

distractors.A: AWS KMS manages encryption keys, not web traffic filtering.
distractors.C: AWS Config tracks resource configuration.
distractors.D: Amazon GuardDuty detects threats from logs but is not a web-request filter.

explanation.exam_pattern: Filter malicious web requests (SQLi/XSS) at layer 7 = AWS WAF.

questions.stem: A company wants a service that continuously analyzes account activity and network logs to detect unusual behavior, such as potentially compromised credentials. Which service fits?

explanation.correct: Amazon GuardDuty is a threat-detection service that analyzes logs (such as CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs) to identify malicious or unusual activity.

distractors.A: Amazon Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities, not behavioral threats in logs.
distractors.B: AWS WAF filters inbound web requests; it does not analyze account activity.
distractors.C: AWS Artifact provides compliance documents.

explanation.exam_pattern: Threat detection from logs and behavior = Amazon GuardDuty.

questions.stem: A security team needs to automatically scan EC2 instances and container images for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure. Which service should they choose?
